title: Separate curated manifest count from generated object count
problem: Catalog page counts are often misread as total database object counts.
recommended_pattern: Report curated YAML manifests separately from generated operational rows. Treat source records, normalized objects, labels, embeddings, review tickets, promotion decisions, and index deltas as database metrics.
storage_boundary: YAML manifests remain curated definitions; Postgres plus pgvector is canonical for high-volume generated rows; JSONL remains staging and object-storage interchange.
quality_gate: A release report must label counts as manifest_count, staged_jsonl_row_count, or canonical_db_row_count.

title: Bootstrap Postgres before bulk primitive generation
problem: Large JSONL shards can accumulate without a queryable canonical store.
recommended_pattern: Run the canonical schema, load staged JSONL through deterministic upsert SQL, then run the object count SQL report before treating the batch as available for search.
storage_boundary: Postgres owns canonical object state; object storage keeps raw snapshots and replayable shards.
quality_gate: A bulk ingestion batch is incomplete until source_record, normalized_object, index_record, and review_ticket counts are reported.

title: Promote only reviewed high-value objects into manifests
problem: Trying to make every generated primitive a YAML manifest makes validation slow and curator review noisy.
recommended_pattern: Use promotion scores and review tickets to decide which generated rows become durable manifests. Keep the rest searchable as generated objects with provenance and freshness metadata.
storage_boundary: Generated candidates stay in normalized_object and related tables until promoted.
quality_gate: Every promoted manifest should reference source provenance or a promotion decision.
